findings.text: public/framework/audio/Recite/Recite.js:22-28 — the unlock also runs on the first tap while the state is "paused" for a reason other than the refusal (a user pause mid-chunk, then tapping Play). It replaces `audio.src` with the silence, so `resume()` (Recite.js:201-202) sees `same` is false and restarts the chunk at 0 instead of continuing. Only run the unlock when `this.state` is not "paused", or when it is paused by the refusal (`/tap/.test(this.error)`); otherwise leave `src` alone.

Recite.js:20-24 — `pointerdown` and `touchend` both fire on one tap, and `unlocked` is only set after the async `play()` resolves, so the second event reassigns `src` and calls `play()` again mid-flight. Add an `unlocking` guard, or drop `pointerdown` (a touch `pointerdown` is not a user activation in Chrome anyway).

public/framework/audio/Recite/readme.md:36 — the Watch out line still describes the old behaviour ("Until then the bar says to tap play"). It should say the first tap anywhere unlocks Recite's `<audio>` and starts a held reply (`unlock_on_tap`, `Recite.SILENCE`). The task folder also holds only requirements.md and review/, with no task record, so a fresh agent cannot see what was tested on a phone.

public/framework/audio/Recite/Recite.test.mjs — no test covers the unlock path (a refused play, then a tap, then the reply starts). That is the single behaviour the owner asked for, so add one using a fake `audio`, or state that it was only checked by hand.
Recite.js:28 depends on the error text containing "tap" (set at Recite.js:86). A shared constant or flag such as `this.refused = true` would not break if the wording changes.

The requirement is met in outline: one change, in Recite.js, and the silence is a data URL, so there is no new file. Nothing was run on a phone, and there are no screenshots, so "met?" is not proven here.

answer.reply: fixed: unlock runs only while idle or after a refusal; a loaded or paused sentence never has its source swapped, and a successful play marks it unlocked
fixed: an `unlocking` flag is set before the async play, so one tap's pointerdown and touchend unlock once (test: 2 plays, not 3)
fixed: readme Watch out line now describes unlock_on_tap
fixed: Recite.test.mjs 'the first tap unlocks a refused reply', 6 checks with a fake <audio> that refuses like a phone; all pass on the test page
noted: the 'tap' text is set in one place (play's NotAllowedError branch); a flag is cleaner, left for the Recite text-prep pass
noted: a real phone is the remaining check; the owner tests it on the walk
